overview: China Jinmao is a Hong Kong-listed, Beijing-headquartered real estate group and a platform enterprise of Sinochem Holdings, a central state-owned enterprise supervised by China's SASAC. Its core business is residential and comprehensive property development (roughly 80% of revenue), complemented by a 'second curve' of investment-property leasing, hotel operations, property management (via separately listed Jinmao Services, HK.00816) and building technology. The group operates almost entirely within mainland China, concentrated in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta regions, and reports in RMB despite its HKD-denominated listing.

business_model.summary: Primarily a project-based property developer that sells residential units (recognised on completion/handover), supplemented by recurring income from investment-property leasing and hotels, fee income from third-party property management (Jinmao Services), and an emerging building-technology/smart-energy services business. Development revenue is lumpy and tied to the land bank, construction and sales cycle; investment property, hotel and services revenue are more recurring but much smaller.

revenue_streams.name: Others (incl. green building tech, building decoration)

business_model.customer_type: B2C homebuyers (development), B2B/institutional tenants (investment properties), B2C/B2B guests (hotels), B2B/B2C property owners (Jinmao Services)
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China only; core cities include Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, Guangzhou, Nanjing, Xi'an, Hangzhou, Chengdu, Wuhan, Qingdao, Chongqing and other tier-1/new tier-1 cities across the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei, Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta regions

competitive_position.market_position: Ranked 8th in China by contracted sales amount in 2025 (RMB113.5bn, up 16% YoY against an industry still contracting), rising to 7th in H1 2026 (RMB57.5bn, +8% YoY); one of the few top-10 developers to grow sales against the industry trend, reflecting its state-owned-enterprise (SOE) funding advantage versus distressed private developers

moat_factors.description: Platform enterprise of Sinochem Holdings (central SASAC-supervised SOE); provides preferential access to bank credit, bond markets and land in a sector where private developers are largely locked out of funding
'Jin Yu Man Tang' product lines (Palace, Pu, Man, Tang series) command premium positioning and strong sell-through in core cities (e.g., top rankings in Xi'an, Nanjing, Xiong'an launches)
Investment properties, hotels, Jinmao Services and building technology provide partial diversification away from pure development, though still a small share of revenue
Issued multiple domestic corporate bonds/MTNs in 2025-2026 at coupons of ~2.3-2.9%, far below what private developers can access

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on property development (~80% of revenue) in a structurally contracting Chinese residential market
High leverage and large land-bank investment requirement (Moody's estimates ~45-50% of contracted sales proceeds reinvested into land)
Effective tax rate elevated (56% in 2025) due to PRC land appreciation tax, compressing net margins
Smaller scale than top-5 peers (Vanke, COLI, CR Land, Poly) despite top-10 ranking
Second-curve businesses (hotels, investment property) still face revenue declines (disposals, REIT spin-off effects)

growth_drivers: Continued replenishment of land reserves in strategic core cities (Beijing, Shanghai) — added >RMB100bn of saleable resources in 2025, RMB29.4bn in H1 2026
Expansion of 'second curve' businesses: premium holding (investment property), quality service (Jinmao Services), and building technology, targeted to accelerate growth beyond pure development
Jinmao Services GFA under management growth (105.7m sqm, +24% revenue in 2025) as a recurring, asset-light fee stream
REIT monetization strategy (CAMC-Jinmao Commercial REIT listed 2024) to recycle capital out of mature investment properties

Potential beneficiary of further China property policy easing/stabilization measures (e.g., relaxation of the 'three red lines' framework, city-specific destocking policies) given SOE funding advantage
Organizational streamlining ('platform + terminal' model, disbanding of regional structures) aimed at improving capital velocity and project turnover ('one crop per year, two crops per year')

business.description: National new-home sales volumes and values continued declining in 2025 (area sold -8.7%, sales value -12.6%); industry still 'bottoming out' with risks not fully cleared per management's own 2026 commentary

RMB611.6m of impairment on properties under development/held for sale recognised in 2025 alone (RMB1,838.6m including JV/associate share); FY2023 saw a ~RMB6.9bn net loss driven largely by such impairments
Hotel revenue declined 5% in 2025 (disposal of Hilton Sanya) and industry prosperity index remains negative; commercial leasing revenue affected by REIT deconsolidation

business.risk: Concentration in a maturing competitive field
business.description: Despite top-8/top-7 ranking, scale remains well below the largest SOE peers (Vanke, COLI, CR Land, Poly)

financial.description: Net debt-to-adjusted-capital ratio of 69% at end-2025 (down to 52% at H1 2026); Moody's estimates leverage near 11x in FY2025, improving only gradually to ~9.2x in 2026
Interest-bearing borrowings of RMB129.0bn at end-2025 (RMB122.8bn at H1 2026); total interest expense RMB6.4bn in 2025 (RMB2.3bn after capitalisation)

Significant amounts due to holding companies (Sinochem Hong Kong Capital Management) factored into adjusted capital; large intercompany loan balances to/from JVs, associates and non-controlling shareholders (RMB25.8bn receivable, RMB29.8bn payable in 2025)
56% effective tax rate in 2025 (up from 50% in 2024) due to PRC land appreciation tax and corporate income tax, compressing bottom-line profitability even when pre-tax profit grows

financial.risk: Negative free cash flow in several recent periods
financial.description: H1 FY2024, H1 FY2025 and FY2024/FY2025 full years show negative free cash flow per company financials; operating cash flow volatile (e.g., -RMB3.6bn FY2024 vs +RMB10.5bn H1 FY2026)

regulatory.description: Business is highly exposed to central and local government policy on home purchase restrictions, mortgage rules, land supply and destocking programs; 2026 Government Work Report language shifted toward 'stabilizing' rather than more aggressive support, and analysts (S&P, MNI) expect continued sector decline through 2026 outside select high-tier cities
Moody's downgraded China Jinmao one notch to Ba3, citing leverage near 11x in FY2025, despite still viewing liquidity as stable and crediting Sinochem's support for funding access

regulatory.risk: Land appreciation tax / local government fiscal pressure
regulatory.description: Rising PRC land appreciation tax contributed to a higher effective tax rate in 2025 and could rise further as local governments seek revenue amid weak land sales

macro.description: Residential demand highly sensitive to consumer confidence, income growth and broader GDP trends; management itself flags homebuyer confidence 'still in the process of recovery'

Heavily reliant on bank borrowings, corporate bonds and MTNs; funding costs and availability are sensitive to PBOC policy and onshore credit conditions, though recent issuance has been at historically low coupons (~2.3-2.9%)
Reports in RMB while listed and dividended partly in HKD; FX translation risk for HK-based investors, though operations are almost entirely domestic RMB-denominated

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Chinese residential property market remains in a prolonged bottoming/adjustment phase; 2025 saw further declines in national new-home sales area (-8.7%) and value (-12.6%). Policy tone has shifted from 'halt the decline and stabilize' toward broader 'stabilization,' with reports that Beijing has eased the 2020 'three red lines' debt-limit framework, but most analysts (S&P, MNI) expect continued overall decline through 2026 with divergence favoring core, high-tier cities and strong SOE developers.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High — residential development is strongly cyclical, tied to the multi-year China property downturn since 2021-2022; investment property/hotel segments are more defensive but still exposed to commercial real estate oversupply and consumer discretionary spending
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — large, mostly floating-rate debt load (only ~RMB28.8bn of RMB129bn total borrowings at fixed rates at end-2025); funding costs directly affect finance costs and net margins
key_input_costs: PRC land appreciation tax and corporate income tax

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 revenue fell 15% YoY to RMB21.4bn and profit attributable to owners fell ~19% to RMB879.2m, with gross margin compressing to 11.6% from 16.2%, even as contracted sales rose 8% YoY to RMB57.5bn and the company's industry sales ranking improved to 7th
Net debt-to-adjusted-capital ratio improved markedly to 52% at 30 June 2026 from 69% at end-2025, alongside a ~4.9% reduction in interest-bearing borrowings to ~RMB122.8bn

Moody's downgraded China Jinmao one notch to Ba3, citing leverage near 11x in FY2025 (vs. its prior ~9.3x projection), while still describing liquidity as stable and crediting continued Sinochem Hong Kong support for funding access and land replenishment

Multiple low-coupon domestic bond/MTN issuances completed through the year (including RMB2.5bn five-year notes at 2.39% in April and another RMB2.5bn tranche in July), reflecting continued SOE funding access even as the broader private-developer sector remains largely shut out of capital markets

Morgan Stanley raised its price target to HK$1.91 (from HK$1.79) and maintained a Buy/Overweight rating following H1 2026 results, citing improving margin and profit trajectory; broader analyst coverage remains predominantly Buy-rated with price targets clustering around HK$1.70-2.14

Full-year 2025 results showed revenue roughly flat (+1% YoY to RMB59.4bn) and profit attributable to owners up 18% YoY to RMB1,253.2m, but net debt-to-adjusted-capital ratio rose to 69% from 67%, and contracted sales grew 16% YoY to RMB113.5bn, rising to 8th in the industry

Continued restructuring of the portfolio: Changsha Jinmao Mall of Splendor deconsolidated into CAMC-Jinmao Commercial REIT (34% retained stake); disposal of Hilton Sanya hotel in H2 2024 reduced hotel segment revenue

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report / FY2025 Annual Report

items.period: FY2026 and medium-term (15th Five-Year Plan period, 2026-2030)
items.notes: Management has explicitly prioritized 'reducing liabilities' ('負債壓降') and reducing reliance on new land investment funded by debt; ratio already improved from 69% (FY2025) to 52% (H1 2026)

items.target: Continue outperforming the market / improving industry ranking
items.notes: H1 2026 contracted sales of RMB57.5bn (+8% YoY) lifted industry ranking to 7th; cumulative 7-month 2026 sales of ~RMB66.7bn (+7.9% YoY); Citigroup expects sales growth to accelerate in Q3 2026

items.target: Selective, core-city focused acquisition with investment discipline
items.notes: H1 2026 added RMB29.4bn of saleable resources at a low average land premium of 1.36% across 12 parcels, concentrated in Beijing, Shanghai and other core cities

items.target: Accelerate growth of premium holding, quality service, and building technology segments to outperform general market trends
items.notes: H1 2026 hotel performance and two commercial projects (Changsha, Qingdao) achieved EBITDA margins >50%; Jinmao Services customer satisfaction improved to 94 points (industry benchmark level)

items.target: HK3.0 cents interim dividend (scrip option offered)
items.notes: Consistent with HK3.0 cents interim dividend paid in H1 2025 and H1 2024; full-year 2025 total dividend also HK3.0 cents (interim only, no final dividend for 2024 or 2025)

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Tao Tianhai's H1 2026 statement describes the real estate industry as still 'bottoming out and consolidating,' with policy tailwinds ('favourable policies frequently introduced') but intensifying market divergence favoring stronger players ('the strong stays strong'). Management explicitly frames 2026-2030 as a critical window for 'financially sound enterprises with leading quality to achieve strategic breakthroughs,' while cautioning that 'the downward inertia of the real estate industry is still continuing, and risks have not yet been cleared' in the short term. Strategic priorities are framed as three battles: performance delivery, product/culture building, and acceleration of the second curve, with increased emphasis on 'tackling existing inventory' and 'reducing liabilities.'

bull_case: State-owned enterprise status under Sinochem Holdings provides a durable funding advantage (low-coupon bond issuance at ~2.3-2.9% in 2026) at a time when most private Chinese developers are effectively locked out of capital markets

One of very few top-10 developers growing contracted sales against the industry trend (+16% in 2025, +8% in H1 2026), with industry ranking improving to 7th, suggesting market-share gains as weaker competitors exit
Deleveraging progress is tangible and recent: net debt-to-adjusted-capital ratio fell from 69% to 52% within six months (H1 2026), alongside absolute debt reduction

Diversification into recurring-revenue second-curve businesses (Jinmao Services, investment properties, REIT monetization, building technology) reduces pure-play exposure to volatile development earnings over time
Analyst sentiment has turned constructive, with Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan and CLSA maintaining Buy ratings and raising price targets through 2026 on improving margins and profit trajectory
bear_case: Underlying Chinese residential property fundamentals remain weak — national sales volumes and values still declining through 2025, with management itself acknowledging risks 'have not yet been cleared'

Leverage remains very high by any absolute standard (Moody's estimates ~11x in FY2025; Ba3 credit rating with a recent downgrade) despite recent improvement, and the company continues to reinvest 45-50% of sales proceeds into land, limiting the pace of deleveraging

H1 2026 results show revenue and profit both declining double digits YoY (-15% revenue, -19% profit) with gross margin compressing sharply (16.2% to 11.6%), even as sales volumes grew — indicating continued pricing/margin pressure on development
FY2023 net loss of ~RMB6.9bn (driven by inventory impairments) illustrates the latent risk that further write-downs could recur if property prices weaken further

High effective tax rate (56% in 2025) from PRC land appreciation tax structurally compresses net margins even when pre-tax operating performance improves, and could worsen if local governments raise land-related levies amid fiscal pressure
